ADFA-5103
The app cannot tell a stopped service from a stopped environment
`pdsm stop` stops the services inside the container; the proot environment keeps running. The app has one runtime signal — an HTTP ping to
/home with a 1.5 s timeout — so "services down, proot alive" and "everything down" are the same observable state, and both render as OFFLINE.
The consequence is not cosmetic: LibraryActivity.canStartServer() reads "not answering" as "nothing is running", so Retry can start a SECOND
proot over a live one — the collision class ADR-4832 documents (shared /tmp, /dev/shm, ports). Reachable after any app restart, because the
handle that would have stopped the first one is a field on an Activity-scoped ServerController.
The environment already tells us it exited — startEnvironment's onProcessExit only logs it. Nothing kills the proot when the app closes.
Detection exists and is tested (EnvironmentProcess). Wiring it needs: the handle per process, "ensure up" not "start", and a boot grace.
ADFA-5104
Module management reads what is installed, and says so — DONE
The screen answered "what is installed" by asking "what is answering", so with the box stopped every module was offered, installed ones
included — an offer that stops the box for hours to rebuild what was there. It reads etc/iiab/local_vars.yml on the rootfs now: the
installer's own record, readable with the services down, and invalidated for free by any reset, restore or clone because it lives inside
the rootfs it describes. Installs only add, so a remembered answer is safe here where a remembered "is it running" would not be.
Three facts, no longer one: a system must exist before modules mean anything; what is installed comes from disk; whether it runs gates
neither. Silence keeps its own name — an unreadable file is "unknown", not "absent". The probe survives, add-only. The list stops hiding
what you have, and the detail agrees with it. GetMoreHub keeps its copy of the probe: add-only there, so not the same defect.
ADFA-5105
Free space is checked before a destructive run — DONE
Sixteen hand-rolled readers, four APIs, two magic margins, and only two of them gated anything — never the wizard install, the reinstall,
restore or reset. A wipe followed by an extract that ran out of disk left a rootfs that would not boot. One reader, one margin, measured on
the filesystem actually written to, and the refusal happens before anything is deleted.
Still open, and no longer named by anyone: a run-level budget that sums a whole queued batch. 5105 put it out of scope deliberately.
ADFA-5110
The build publishes the uncompressed rootfs size — DONE
Every free-space estimate was built on the compressed artifact size, because that is what rootfs_sizes.csv and the meta4 carry. The extract
writes the larger uncompressed tree, so every estimate under-counted — which is what made 5105's preflight need a real figure.
The builder had the tree in hand already. Producer only: it publishes a sidecar the app can read before downloading or wiping anything.
ADFA-5106
A download measured in hours has no durable record
Content sessions live in static memory inside their services. If the process dies mid-download, the job state and the wishlist that ordered
it both go, and the user comes back to a screen that knows nothing about work that may have run for an afternoon.
ADFA-4874 found this on 27 July, deferred it to a background-jobs monitor that was never opened, and closed the same day. Unowned until now.
NO TICKET YET
A finished run leaves no evidence it happened
A LIVE run is meant to be left alone, so the user usually arrives after it ended and finds a bare "3 Done". The rate is dropped at completion
by design — rateSuffix is called only from the not-complete branch — and "838 MB · 32 MB/s · 4 min" is the only thing that tells a real
download from a no-op. Split out of the UX-contract item because it is not a token: it is instrumentation, in three services with three
different starting points, and pretending otherwise kept it amber on a card it did not belong to.
Courses can do it today (KolibriSeedState has bytes). ZIM has no clock at all. Books has neither bytes nor speed on its service. The only
start timestamp in main/ is KolibriSeedRepository.startedAtMs, private and unreachable from the row renderer. Also here: the maps card
cannot show "adding content", because its progress belongs to the module queue rather than to a content stream.
NO TICKET YET
Replacing the system, and the installer that does it — no ticket on purpose
Moved out of ADFA-4758, which had absorbed it. Neither item is a fix: they are capability the app does not have, on top of a flow
that works. Recorded here so they are picked up on their own terms rather than as somebody else's leftovers.
Two separately invoked installers. One ACTION_START becomes five pipelines through four booleans set by three unrelated senders.
Content-only backup, so a reinstall at another tier can keep what the user added. From zero: the box wipes and rewrites.
Not blocked by this: the tier picker reports success while doing nothing when a rootfs directory exists — implemented and wrong
today, so it is a bug with its own ticket, not part of the work above.
CARRIED, NOT BLOCKING
Found in the last two days; recorded so they are met on purpose
The Books "downloads" link is the last fragment hosting itself. Needs an index that can be opened with nothing in flight.
The three live REST streams can still start together: one provisioner drains asynchronously, so the others see no session yet.
Order: 5061 first, 4954 alongside it (done), then 5074 (done), then 5062. 5074 came before 5062 because 5062 migrates the
SetupProgressActivity key switch — work thrown away if the hosting changed after it.
4758 closed on its real objective: software and content are chosen separately. What it had absorbed was never its goal — see the card below.
The canvas is not page-sized on purpose. Grow it when something new belongs here rather than dropping an item to make room.
